title: Observe installed Claude runtime from production Windows facts
description: Objective: supply the missing production host adapter behind Claude runtime pinning. Fresh measurement at committed HEAD 6ca5da07 found `probeClaudeRuntime` and `prepareClaudeRuntimePin`, but no production `ClaudeProbePort`/`ClaudeRuntimeFactsPort`; all callers are tests or recovery inventory, while task-6cbff010 can currently succeed only by injecting `{fs,facts,clock}` from its test. Deliverable: an internal @moe/runner Windows host module that takes only bounded plain installed-runtime configuration, resolves and streams the complete native Claude closure, obtains version and platform facts through a shell-free bounded Windows process/OS boundary, feeds the production capability/observation builders, and returns immutable current facts/observation or an existing stable RUNTIME/Windows-process refusal. Unproven capabilities remain UNSUPPORTED. No caller-supplied observation, digest, version, capability answer, filesystem capability, clock, or process seam may become authority. This producer is consumed by task 6f8f1e5c (server-owned pin-request hydration; create immediately after this task) and ultimately task-6cbff010. NOT in scope: grant consumption, daemon/store orchestration, provider work launch, review, or final acceptance. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-host-runtime.ts, claude-host-runtime.js, and claude-host-runtime.test.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: On Windows, the production adapter resolves a bounded local installed root/executable, streams closure digests, performs a shell-free bounded version/facts observation, and returns a production-built immutable ProviderRuntimeObservation plus ClaudeRuntimeFacts whose digest and truth class recompute.

Malformed, non-Windows, missing/reparse/escaping, unreadable, timed-out, malformed-output, and drifted observations fail closed with the exact existing RUNTIME or Windows-process reason code and refusing layer; no case upgrades UNKNOWN/UNSUPPORTED to PROVEN.
Only capabilities proved by the production observation are SUPPORTED; a version-only probe leaves every other capability explicitly UNSUPPORTED, with generated cases asserting a positive count.

Tests exercise the production surface and include a real Windows conformance leg (native Windows or `/init` bridge) plus mutation drills proving closure hashing, fresh version/platform facts, and fail-closed classification are load-bearing.
All three owned files are the only changed paths, each production source is below 250 physical lines, and runner/repo typecheck plus a nonzero runner test suite pass.
taskRails: Use the existing `probeClaudeRuntime`, observation builder, runtime-pin filesystem, and Windows process boundary internally; do not reimplement their authority or publish their injectable ports.
The public result may expose facts/data, never filesystem/process/clock capabilities; input is bounded plain data and error messages do not echo runtime paths, argv, environment, or secrets.
TDD every behavior; every failure test asserts exact stable reason code and layer, generated sweeps assert a positive case count, and mutation drills target the production surface.
Keep the TypeScript production file below 250 physical lines, the .js bridge one line, and commit only the three explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED FIRST, honoured literally on the two gaps the reject named. The sweep's existing 16 cases stand as QA verified them; this step adds what was missing and proves each addition RED against the PREVIOUS production bytes before any fix.

GAP A — the no-echo rail was asserted by NOTHING (reject item on test:66). refusalOf read ok/observation/profile/truthClass/code and never looked at `message`, which is exactly why the leak shipped green. Added to refusalOf, so it now covers EVERY case in the sweep rather than one bespoke test:
- `message` must be a string, non-empty, and <= MAX_REFUSAL_MESSAGE_CHARS (200) — long enough for a category sentence, far too short to carry an install path.
- PATH_SHAPED = /[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|\\\\[^\\]|\/(?:tmp|var|home|Users|private)\//u must NOT match. This rejects the SHAPE (drive-qualified, UNC, POSIX absolute), so it fails on any location rather than only on the one path a fixture happened to use.
- New `inputSecrets(input)` collects the case's own string inputs and asserts none appears in the message. The shape regex and the echo check catch different failure modes: a shape check cannot see an echo that arrives in another form, and an input check cannot see a path this case never supplied.

GAP B — DoD 2 and plan step 2 both name "an unreadable file"; the sweep had none (missing, directory, reparse, escape and not-an-image are all distinct conditions). Added "the executable cannot be read": a real, contained, plain file made unreadable with a REAL deny ACE (`icacls <path> /deny <USERNAME>:(R)`), not a stubbed fs error. Fixture is VALID AT EVERY EARLIER LAYER per this file's own doctrine — it exists, it is a plain file, it is inside the root, it crosses no reparse point — so the read failure is the property under test and nothing earlier can answer for it. CASES.length assertion bumped 16 -> 17 as the reject instructed.

implementationPlan.description:
PRODUCTION PART 2 — validated streamed closure, twice, with drift detection. Use `inspectSources(fs, candidates, realRoot)` from claude-runtime-source.ts with an `fs` obtained from `createNodeClaudeRuntimeFs()` (claude-runtime-pin-fs.ts:61), constructed INSIDE this module and never accepted from the caller. This is the primitive task-ff589abd was created to deliver, and it is the reason this task was blocked: it performs the segment/reparse/containment walk and returns the streamed `sha256` in one pass, so you never hash a candidate before validating it. Do NOT copy the private segment walk into this module — that would create parallel authority and violate task rail 1.
Run the inspection TWICE, once before the version probe of step 5 and once after, and require the resulting `SourceEntry` digests to be identical. A mismatch returns `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_SOURCE_DRIFT`. The two-pass shape is the point: a single pass cannot tell a stable installation from one swapped underneath you while the probe was running, and DoD 2 requires drifted observations to fail closed. Feed the second pass's entries — not the first's — into the observation as `resolvedRuntimeClosure`, so the bytes reported are the bytes that survived the probe window.
implementationPlan.note:
THE REJECT'S SECURITY FIX LANDS HERE — this is the step that owns inspectClosure, where the echo originated.

STRUCTURE FROM ba361b3 STANDS, re-confirmed at HEAD: `inspectSources(fs, candidates, realRoot)` with `fs` from `createNodeClaudeRuntimeFs()` constructed INSIDE the module and never accepted from the caller; no private segment walk copied in (task rail 1); inspection run TWICE around the probe; digest mismatch returns CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_SOURCE_DRIFT; and the SECOND pass's entries feed `resolvedRuntimeClosure`, so the bytes reported are the bytes that survived the probe window.

THE LEAK, precisely. inspectClosure forwarded the inspector's own prose to the public surface at two sites:
  if ("code" in candidates) return refuse(candidates.code, candidates.message);
  return "code" in inspected ? refuse(inspected.code, inspected.message) : inspected;
`inspectOne` builds every message from `const named = JSON.stringify(candidate.path)` (claude-runtime-source.ts:181) and `refuse()` stores its second argument verbatim on the public `.message`. So every closure-layer refusal published the absolute installed executable path — the task rail 2 violation. Measured before the fix: `"C:\\Users\\Yaron\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\moe-host-runtime-34kpVj\\absent.exe" is not a plain contained file`.

THE FIX, exactly the shape the reject prescribed ("keep the code and layer, substitute your own fixed category sentence"). Added `CLOSURE_REFUSAL_SENTENCES`, a hand-written frozen map from code to a fixed sentence, and `closureRefusal(code)` which calls the SAME `refuse` helper. Both sites now pass only the code. Nothing diagnostic is lost — the code and the layer still carry the precise reason; only the location is withheld. `refuse()` stamps layer=RUNTIME and truthClass=UNKNOWN itself, so replacing the message cannot disturb either, which the sweep's code+layer assertions confirm still pass on all 17 cases.

WHY Partial<Record<...>> WITH A FALLBACK rather than an exhaustive map: `ClaudeRuntimePinErrorCode` spans the whole pin vocabulary including PIN_COLLISION, PIN_COPY_FAILED and PIN_DESTINATION_MISMATCH, which the closure inspection cannot return. An exhaustive map would force meaningless entries for unreachable codes. The eight reachable ones are mapped by hand; anything else falls back to "the declared runtime closure could not be verified", which is still a fixed literal — so an upstream code added later degrades to generic prose, never to a leak. Disclosed as a deliberate trade rather than left for a reviewer to find.

VERIFIED, same test bytes either side of the production change: EXIT=1 "Tests 5 failed | 15 passed (20)" before, EXIT=0 "Tests 20 passed (20)" after. Because the test file was identical across both runs, that delta isolates the production fix and nothing else — the assertion is killed by the bug and revived by the fix, which is the only evidence that proves it is load-bearing.

`grep -n 'inspected.message\|candidates.message'` over the module now returns 0 occurrences.

implementationPlan.description:
PRODUCTION PART 3 — shell-free bounded version observation through the real Job boundary. Obtain the reported version by launching the validated executable with a single `--version` argument through `openWindowsProcessBoundary(request, { timeoutMs })` from platform/windows/windows-boundary.ts. That is the production Windows process seam: it is broker-mediated, job-object bounded, and structurally shell-free — do NOT reach for child_process, a shell, or `.cmd`/`.bat` indirection. Note the boundary is SYNCHRONOUS on its refusal path and returns `WindowsProcessBoundary | WindowsProcessUnknown`; a `WindowsProcessUnknown` is already a stable coded refusal at its own layer, so return it unchanged rather than re-wrapping it into a RUNTIME code and erasing which layer answered.
On the success path, read `providerStdout` with a BOUNDED accumulation (cap the bytes you retain, matching the existing `MAX_RUNTIME_TEXT_CHARS` discipline in claude-observation.ts) and await `completed`; always `close()` the boundary on every exit path including the throw path, so a failed parse cannot leak a broker process. Parse the version text conservatively — a shape you do not recognise yields a refusal, never a guessed string and never null-as-success. Pass an explicit bounded `timeoutMs`; the module's `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` is 30 minutes, far too long for a version probe.
Separately derive `PlatformIdentity` — `{os, arch, osVersion}` — from `node:os` inside this module, then validate it through the EXISTING `platformHostRejection` / `readHostIdentity` / `MAX_PLATFORM_IDENTITY_CHARS` helpers in platform/platform-contract.ts rather than writing your own bounds check. There is no `observeWindowsPlatform` producer in this repo (measured: linux-observation.ts and macos-observation.ts exist, no Windows sibling); reading `node:os` here is the production host boundary, and the clock is likewise constructed internally, never injected.
implementationPlan.note:
Bytes from ba361b3 STAND, untouched by this session's fix. QA verified this surface good; re-confirmed at HEAD rather than re-derived, and re-run green.

CONFIRMED AT HEAD:
- The only process seam is `openWindowsProcessBoundary(...)` with a single `--version` argv. No child_process, no shell, no .cmd/.bat indirection anywhere in the module.
- The boundary's SYNCHRONOUS refusal path is returned UNCHANGED (`if (!("providerStdout" in boundary)) return boundary;`), so a WindowsProcessUnknown keeps its own code and its own layer instead of being restamped as a RUNTIME code. The sweep proves this is live, not aspirational: the "not a loadable image" case asserts code PROCESS_BOUNDARY_BROKER_REFUSED at layer BROKER_NATIVE, i.e. a foreign layer really does answer and really is preserved.
- stdout accumulation is bounded by MAX_RUNTIME_TEXT_CHARS.
- `close()` runs in a `finally`, so every exit path including a throw releases the broker.
- Version parsing is conservative: VERSION_PATTERN, plus isBoundedLabel; an unrecognised shape refuses rather than guessing or treating null as success. The sweep exercises this with a real node.exe copy, which answers `--version` cleanly with `v24.16.0` — a genuine clean execution whose output is simply not this provider's shape.
- Timeout is explicit and bounded: DEFAULT_VERSION_TIMEOUT_MS 10s, MAX 600s, never the boundary's own 30-minute default.
- PlatformIdentity is derived from node:os inside the module and validated through the EXISTING readHostIdentity helper, not a hand-rolled bounds check. Clock constructed internally, never injected.

RELEVANT TO MY CHANGE, checked rather than assumed: the refusals on this path — `invalid("probe did not exit cleanly, so no version was observed")` and `invalid("probe printed output that is not the version shape this provider reports")` — were ALREADY fixed literals and carry no path, argv or environment value. So the new no-echo assertion in refusalOf passes on the timeout and malformed-output cases without any production change here. That is worth stating explicitly: the leak was confined to the closure path, and I verified the probe path independently instead of assuming one fix covered both.

PASSED_ENVIRONMENT stays the allowlisted pair (SYSTEMROOT, PATH) and is never echoed back out of a failure path — which the new assertion now actively polices, since an environment value reaching a message would be caught by the same PATH_SHAPED check.

implementationPlan.description:
PRODUCTION PART 4 — compose capabilities, observation, and facts from what was actually proved. Build a `ClaudeProbeReport` (claude-capabilities.ts:97) populated ONLY from this run's evidence: `resolvedRuntimeClosure` from the second inspection pass, `reportedVersion` from the probe, `pinningMethod` set to `CONTENT_ADDRESSED_COPY` (a validated native executable closure can be content-addressed and copied — assert in the test that it is NOT `UNSUPPORTED`, since that member exists precisely so a wrapper can read a definite negative). EVERY other field — structuredSample, rawSampleBase64, cancelObservation, processTreeObservation, runEnumeration, tokenizer, declaredContextLimit, helpText, resumeClaim — stays null. A version-only probe proves version and pin method and nothing else.
Wrap that report in a `ClaudeProbePort` constructed internally and pass it to the existing `probeClaudeRuntime({ port, clock, platformIdentity })` (claude-probe.ts:56), which runs `assessCapabilities` and `buildProviderRuntimeObservation` for you. Do not call the builders directly around it and do not re-implement their authority — task rail 1. Note the port is INTERNAL: it must not appear on this module's public surface.
Derive `ClaudeRuntimeFacts` (claude-runtime-pin.ts:41) as `{ platformIdentity, reportedVersion, adapterCapabilitySchemaDigest }`, taking the digest from the profile's `capabilitySchemaDigest` — never from caller input. Freeze the returned observation and facts. The expected outcome, which the tests must pin as an exact set rather than a spot check: of the ELEVEN members of `CLAUDE_CAPABILITIES`, exactly TWO are SUPPORTED — `PIN_METHOD` (proof `PIN_METHOD_RECORD`) and `VERSION_REPORT` (proof `VERSION_RECORD`) — and the remaining NINE are UNSUPPORTED with proof `NONE`, with `contextPolicy` HOLD_UNKNOWN because no limit was declared. Assert the SUPPORTED count is exactly 2 and the UNSUPPORTED count exactly 9, and assert the records equal the full eleven-member vocabulary in vocabulary order — a sweep that generates zero cases, or that spot-checks two members, passes while testing nothing.

REAL WINDOWS CONFORMANCE LEG, with no vacuous-skip escape. Add to the test file a leg that runs the whole path against the genuinely installed runtime — the real `claude.exe`, the real release broker, real streamed digests, a real `--version`. The file must execute meaningful assertions on EVERY host, because a leg that quietly skips reports zero cases and passes while proving nothing:
- when `process.platform === "win32"` and both host preconditions from step 1 hold, assert the PROVEN arm end to end: a non-null `reportedVersion`, a `resolvedRuntimeClosure` of exactly one EXECUTABLE entry whose sha256 is a 64-char lowercase hex string, a recomputing `observationDigest`, `truthClass` PROVEN, and the exact 2-SUPPORTED / 9-UNSUPPORTED capability split. Assert a POSITIVE receipt count for the cases this leg generated, so a silently emptied leg reddens.
- when not on win32, assert the refusal arm instead: `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` at layer RUNTIME. That is a real assertion about production behavior, not a skip.
- when on win32 but a precondition is genuinely absent, assert the corresponding stable refusal (`PROCESS_BOUNDARY_BROKER_UNRESOLVED` for a missing broker) rather than skipping or, worse, asserting a fabricated pass.
MEASURED HAZARD, disclose it rather than chase it: the foreign `claude-launcher.windows.test.ts:178` currently gets `truthClass UNKNOWN` at `layer OUTPUT` where it wants PROVEN, on a real Windows launch on this same host. That is about launch OUTPUT truth, a different subject from this task's version observation — but if your PROVEN arm also comes back UNKNOWN, do NOT weaken the assertion to match. planningNotes.risks:
1) THE 250-LINE CAP IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT AND THERE IS NO FOURTH FILE. Platform gate + input hardening + two-pass inspection + boundary probe + parse + facts/observation composition is a lot for one source, and the three owned paths forbid splitting. Mitigations: compose through existing primitives rather than re-deriving, and keep EVERY fixture and helper in the .test.ts (uncapped). If it still will not fit, `moe.request_replan` — do not silently overflow and do not add an unowned file. Measure with `grep -c '' <file>`; PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts.

2) THE BOUNDARY'S DEFAULT TIMEOUT IS 30 MINUTES. `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000`. A version probe that inherits it turns a hung runtime into a half-hour test hang rather than a `PROCESS_BOUNDARY_LAUNCH_TIMED_OUT` refusal. Pass an explicit bounded `timeoutMs` and cover the timeout case.

3) RESOURCE LEAK ON THE THROW PATH. The boundary spawns a real broker process. `close()` must run on every exit path including a failed version parse; otherwise a red test leaves a broker alive and poisons the rest of a `fileParallelism` run.

4) THREE LAYERS CAN REFUSE HERE — RUNTIME (claude-runtime-pin-closure), the observation builder's CLAUDE_OBSERVATION_* codes, and WINDOWS_PROCESS_* at its own layer. An assertion pinning only a code, or only 'not ok', silently detaches the moment a different layer starts answering first. Pin code AND layer everywhere, and build each fixture valid at every earlier layer so the intended guard is the one that speaks. Resist the temptation to re-wrap a `WindowsProcessUnknown` into a RUNTIME code — that erases which layer refused.

5) MEASURED FOREIGN RED, AND A WARNING SIGN INSIDE IT. `claude-launcher.windows.test.ts:178` currently gets `truthClass UNKNOWN` at `layer OUTPUT` where it expects PROVEN, on a real Windows launch on this very host. Foreign — disclose, do not repair. But note the shape: if this task's PROVEN arm also returns UNKNOWN, that is a real finding to report, NOT an invitation to weaken the assertion. A proof narrowed to accept UNKNOWN certifies nothing, and epic rail 4 keeps unverifiable evidence at UNKNOWN by design.

6) BRIDGE BYTES ARE BYTE-COMPARED by the repo's bridge guard. `export * from "./claude-host-runtime.ts";` plus a single LF — CRLF or a trailing blank line lands the file in the guard's `wrongContent` set instead of fixing `missing`.

7) EXIT 0 IS NOT EVIDENCE. Read the `Test Files`/`Tests` count lines; require them strictly above the 64/2148 baseline. Never `;`-chain a gate (only the last status survives) and never pipe into tail (tail's status is reported).

8) SHARED WORKTREE, ACTIVE. HEAD moved three times during this planning session (1357062 -> 91fc622 -> cf137c6). Re-check `git status --porcelain` immediately before committing, commit by explicit three-path pathspec, verify with `git show --stat`. Revert every mutation drill via `git checkout --` and confirm clean — a foreign whole-tree completion hook can otherwise commit your drill.

9) DO NOT OVERCLAIM WHAT THIS PRODUCES. Per the prior architect's handoff: this module supplies fresh launch-time facts and a narrow two-capability observation. It does NOT establish the full Foundation provider admission profile, and the completion note should not imply otherwise.
